title: GGUF block matrices (Q8_0, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS, IQ3_S, Q6_K) multiplied on the device
description: The projections slot over a GGUF's stored blocks: each matrix stays on the device in its stored GGUF format (format gguf:KIND, tensors {weight: uint8 [rows][row_bytes], cols}), decoded to BF16 a chunk of output rows at a time (code/gguf_blocks.py, bit for bit gguf-py's dequantize) and multiplied by torch's BF16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation; calls of up to 8 rows are padded to 8, so a decode row's bits are its own whatever rows share the call. Plain BF16 matrices (format bf16) too. Prompt rows (calls of more than 8 rows) multiply in FP8 E4M3 with row-wise scales on the activations and the decoded weight rows (prompt fp8, the default), or BF16; decode rows in BF16.

chunk_mib.description: MiB of decoded BF16 rows a matmul holds at once

prompt.description: prompt rows' activations: the stored GGUF formats' own (int8 units of 32 with an FP32 scale, the int8 tensor cores straight from the blocks), FP8 with row-wise scales, or BF16

gemv_rows.description: prompt calls of up to this many rows run as stored-block GEMV passes of 8 rows (BF16 activations); longer ones decode the matrix for the tensor cores

decode.description: decode rows' activations: the stored GGUF formats' own (int8 units of 32 with an FP32 scale, integer dot products), or BF16 with every weight decoded to FP32

q8_layout.description: Q8_0 matrices (but an embedding) as stored, or repacked at load into the same bytes in an aligned order (codes, then scales) for 16-byte loads; aligned takes stored decode and prompt activations
